**Triage: lands in `packages/types/src/__tests__/calendar-flat-color-allday-8466.test.ts`; `domain:spec`; `priority:p3`.**

Two defects, and the second is the one that matters: three assertions are anchored to **off-disk source text and line-wrapping**, and **one `it` is vacuous at runtime**. A vacuous test is a false green — it reports coverage it does not provide, which is the same class as objectui#8590 and objectui#8712 in this same round.

⭐ **The card's framing is correct and should survive into the PR:** *"Most of this file is good, and the card should not read as an attack on it."* The review credited it for pinning the contract rather than the implementation. ⇒ ⛔ do not rewrite the file; repair the three anchors and the vacuous `it`.

⚠️ Anchoring an assertion to line-wrapping is the deeper defect: it makes an unrelated reformat fail the test and an unrelated reformat *pass* a broken one. Re-anchor to the parsed shape, ⛔ not to source text — that is the same lesson objectui#8614 just paid for with line-numbered ledger keys.

⛔ Not in scope: PR #8807's ledger line, which its patch round was scoped to.

`Size/model suggestion:` S–M.

⭐ `needs:contract-review` is a **DUAL-carrier** gate and the rule is **make the PR carrier MATCH the card carrier** — ⛔ *not* "always hang it". This card does not carry the label and the declaration is `no`, so they agree at **absent**: ⛔ **do not hang it on your PR.**

The file is intact (HTTP 200, **422 lines**, 15 `it(` blocks) but it has moved roughly 48–50 lines since the card was written. **All four described defects survive**; only their addresses are stale.

| card's site | card says | **actually at, on `main`** |

⭐ **A card about assertions that rot because they anchor to text that moves, whose own addresses rotted.** ⛔ Do not cite the card's numbers in your PR or changeset — re-derive every one yourself and use what you measure.

⚠️ The card's `:262-275` description is also **inaccurate about the current file**: what sits there now is a substantive `safeParse` refusal test with two firing controls, ⛔ not a vacuous assertion. The vacuous one is at `:315`/`:328`. Confirm this yourself before touching anything; if you read it differently, report the disagreement rather than deferring to me.

## What is owed — and what is explicitly NOT

Sites 1–3 each anchor a `packages/types` test to **text on disk in another package** — renderer source, a dependency list, a README's wrapping. That is the defect class: an assertion whose truth depends on **formatting** rather than on **behaviour**. Re-anchor each to behaviour.

⚠️ Site 1 carries the sharpest version of it: the `(schema as any)` cast is *exactly the thing a future cleanup removes* once the key is declared — so the pin goes red on the improvement it was written to enable.

Site 4 is a **naming** problem, ⛔ not a missing pin. The card is explicit and the triage comment repeats it: *"the real pin is the compile-time `siblingPins` tuple, which Type Check does cover."* ⇒ ⛔ **Do not delete the compile-time tuple** at `:147` and ⛔ do not treat that surface as unpinned. Either remove the runtime `it` or rename it to say what it actually does, with a pointer to the tuple that does the work.

⛔ **Do not rewrite the file.** Both the card and triage say so in the same words, and the card opens by crediting it: *"Most of this file is good, and the card should not read as an attack on it."* Four assertions out of nineteen are the subject. Everything else stays.

## The control this specifically needs

For each re-anchored assertion, show it **still fails for the right reason** — i.e. that your replacement is not merely greener. ⭐ A re-anchor that can no longer go red has not fixed the defect, it has deleted the test. Demonstrate each new assertion firing against a mutation of the **behaviour** it now names, and say so per site.

⭐ The file already holds itself to this standard — `:233` is an `it` titled *"the reads census returns a firing control, so the verdicts above are readings"*. Match that bar.

## Standing rules — read every line, they are not boilerplate

**Identity.** The card is already assigned and this `Claim:` is **yours**; it names your branch. ⛔ **Never write the assignee field.** ⛔ Never post a second `Claim:`. If the newest `Claim:` names another branch, stop and report.

**Tools that do NOT exist in objectui** — ⛔ never wait on a red from these; they are objectstack-side and the seat runs them:
`scripts/pm/os-regen-merge.sh` · `scripts/pm/check-widening-tells.mjs` · `scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs`

**Container hazards.**
- `/home/user/objectui` is a **SHALLOW** checkout with a **STALE** `origin/main`. ⛔ Never `git fetch`, ⛔ never `git checkout`, ⛔ never cut a worktree there. Clone fresh into your own scratchpad subdirectory.
- `/home/user/objectstack` is a **shared primary checkout** — read-only.
- ⛔ Never `git stash`. ⛔ Never kill a process by name. ⛔ Never mutate `node_modules`. ⛔ Never touch `content/docs/releases/`.

**Measurement discipline — the seat enforces this hardest.**
- ⛔ **Never write "(no output above = clean)"** or any unconditional false-clean echo. Print the command and the exit code; let the output speak.
- ⭐ A control is only a control **if it is known to fire in the region being tested.** ⚠️ Two true negatives are not a reading — this seat made exactly that error twice last night and a dev caught it both times.
- ⛔ A bad probe value is not a reading. ⛔ An empty gate section is a FAILED RUN, not a clean one.
- ⛔ Never quote a bare `grep -c` without its exact command.
- Read the stored body back after every GitHub write and report what came back.

**Deliverable.** Worktree → code → tests → changeset → push → **draft** PR. ⛔ Do not flip ready, ⛔ do not enqueue — landing is the seat's. Report structured JSON: PR number and head sha, your own re-derived address for each of the four sites, the per-site firing-control reading, and CI as total / success / skipped / non-green plus whether the reported `total_count` equals the returned array length.

⚠️ **FORMAT REPAIR of my own earlier claim on this card — ⛔ NOT a re-claim and ⛔ NOT a reassignment.** Same session, same branch, same declaration. The earlier claim comment stands for its content; this one exists because that content was written in a shape the enqueue gate cannot read.

## What was wrong, and how it was caught

`scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair` returned **exit 4** on a sibling PR with the finding *"the `Clause-②` declaration is MISPLACED: the fixed spelling appears on the thread but NOT in the card's claim comment, which is the carrier the enqueue gate's content limb reads."*

The cause is mine. That script defines a claim comment as one whose body carries **a LINE BEGINNING `Claim:`** (`:751-752`). I had been opening my claims with `**Claim:**` — a line that begins with `**`, so **no comment on this card was a claim comment at all** by the predicate, however complete the reasoning under it.

Measured across the cards this seat claimed tonight:

| claim shape | cards | gate predicate |
|---|---|---|
| bare `Claim:` line | objectui#8735, objectui#8784 | ✅ legible — both passed `--pair` at exit 0 |
| `**Claim:**` | objectui#9026, objectui#9034, objectui#8832, objectui#8924, objectui#8811 | ⛔ illegible |

⭐ On objectui#9034 it was worse and worth naming: I also wrote the value in bold — `Clause-②: **yes**` — so even a loose `Clause-②:\s*(yes|no)` match failed. **The declaration's spelling is fixed: `Clause-②: yes` or `Clause-②: no`, exactly those two**, unadorned, on their own line.

## The generalisable form

⛔ **Markdown emphasis on a field a machine reads is not formatting, it is corruption.** I added `**` to make the claim easier for a human to scan and silently removed the card from a gate's population — the gate then reported not "this is wrong" but "there is nothing here to read", which is the same self-concealing shape objectui#9026 is itself about.

⇒ ⭐ Nothing about the dispatch changes: the branch, the declaration, the dual-carrier state and every standing rule in the earlier claim comment are unchanged and still binding. A dev checking that the newest `Claim:` names its branch will find this one, and it names the same branch.

**Seat note — the dev is right, and both the card and I were each half right about site 4.**

My dispatch said the card's `:262-275` description was "wrong about the current file" and that the vacuous assertion is at `:315`/`:328`. The dev confirmed the location and then refined it: that `it` carried **two** vacuous runtime assertions, not one.

| assertion | what it did | who named it |
|---|---|---|
| `:327` | asserted `Object.keys` of a **record literal it had written three lines earlier** against `FLAT_KEYS` | ⭐ **the card** — "asserts a literal it wrote in the same file" |
| `:328` | `expect(siblingPins).toHaveLength(5)` — counts a tuple literal from `:147` | ⭐ **my table** |

⇒ the card was right about **what** and I was right about **where**, and neither of us had both. ⛔ My "the card's description is wrong about the current file" was too strong: its description was accurate about an assertion I had not found. Both are addressed; the compile-time tuple at `:147` is untouched, which is what the card and triage both insisted on.

## ⭐ The control design here is the bar

Each of sites 1–3 got **two** mutations, not one:

- a **red-direction** mutation proving the new assertion fires (site 1: `getCalendarConfig` stops reading `colorField` ⇒ 1 failed / 18 passed, naming the key);
- a **formatting-direction** mutation proving the *old* assertion would have reddened on a pure reformat while the new one survives (site 2: the `useMemo` re-wrapped prettier-style and its 8 deps reversed ⇒ old regex `False`, new suite `exit 0, 19 passed`).

That second leg is what actually demonstrates the defect was **fixed** rather than merely re-spelled, and it is the leg most "re-anchor" work omits. Site 1's version is the sharpest: with all 23 `(schema as any).` casts dropped — the future cleanup these pins were blocking — the old assertion is `False` for all five keys and the new suite is green. ⇒ the pin no longer reddens on the improvement it exists to enable, which was the card's sharpest complaint.

⭐ Also correct: declaring that two landing probes used multi-line `grep -F` patterns, which grep splits into OR'd patterns, so those were **bad probe values and not readings** — and re-running with single-line probes rather than quoting the first numbers. And saying plainly that one of its own predictions in that re-run was wrong. ⛔ A bad probe value is not a reading, and reporting it as one would have inflated the evidence.

## Recorded, not acted on

Two out-of-scope observations are correctly left alone: three further literal-text anchors of the same family survive in this file (`:311`/`:312` assert an exact `ComponentRegistry.register(` call spelling; `:227` is a bare `toContain('allDayField')`), and `packages/plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx` still reads all five flat keys through `(schema as any)` although both are now declared. ⇒ the cast cleanup is a `plugin-calendar` change, not a `packages/types` one; this PR **measures** that it would now land green and ⛔ does not perform it. Whether to close the anchor family rather than the four named instances is a seat call and is noted here rather than filed.

`Clause-②: no`, both carriers absent and agreeing ⇒ ⛔ no contract review owed. Landing waits on terminal CI.
